subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: The nasal index is a ratio calculated by dividing the width of the nasal aperture by its height and multiplying by 100. This metric is frequently used to assess which component of the biological profile?
questions.explain: The nasal index and overall nasal morphology (e.g., nasal width, presence of a nasal spine) are classic indicators historically used by anthropologists to infer biological ancestry.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: During a skeletal analysis, it is observed that the victim possesses spatulate incisors, circular-shaped eye orbits, and a pronounced, sharp nasal spine. These skeletal markers most closely align with which ancestral profile?
questions.explain: Traits characteristic of European ancestry typically include sloping eye orbits (often described as circular/aviator-shaped), a narrow nasal opening, a sharp anterior nasal spine, and relatively flat facial profiles.
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: Which of the following craniofacial traits is most frequently found in skulls of African descent?
options: Pronounced facial prognathism and a wide, rounded nasal aperture
A prominent, sharp anterior nasal spine and narrow nasal root
A flat facial profile and circular eye orbits
questions.explain: Traits generally associated with African ancestry include a wider, rounded nasal aperture, a lack of a sharp nasal spine, rectangular eye orbits, and facial prognathism (forward projection of the lower face).
questions.subject: Forensic Anthropology

questions.q: An examination of a victim's dentition reveals deep concavities on the lingual (tongue-facing) side of the central incisors. This distinct anatomical trait is called 'shovel-shaped incisors' and is most strongly associated with individuals of:
questions.explain: Shovel-shaped incisors—incisors with thick marginal ridges forming a scoop or shovel shape on the back side—are heavily expressed in populations of Asian and Native American/Indigenous descent.
